title: Inspect gravel tires, rims and tubeless condition
summary: Evaluate the tire/rim system before adjusting pressure or troubleshooting a tubeless setup.

steps.title: Confirm the real tire and rim system
steps.instruction: Identify the tire size/construction, rim dimensions and whether both components are approved for the intended tube or tubeless configuration.
steps.why: Visual similarity does not prove tire/rim/tubeless compatibility.
steps.warning: Do not assume tubeless compatibility unless the actual tire and rim system supports it.
steps.check: The intended tire/rim configuration is supported by the actual component information.

steps.title: Inspect casing, tread and bead seating
steps.instruction: Look around the complete tire for cuts, abrasion, exposed casing, bulges or uneven bead seating. Inspect the visible rim for dents, cracks or damage.
steps.why: Pressure adjustment cannot compensate for structural tire or rim damage.
steps.warning: Do not continue riding a structurally damaged tire or rim until it is correctly assessed.
steps.check: No obvious structural tire/rim damage is visible.

steps.title: Set pressure from the real system and conditions
steps.instruction: Measure current pressure and adjust only within the tire/rim limits, accounting for rider/bike load, surface, tire volume and setup. Recheck after adjustment.
steps.why: Useful gravel pressure depends on more variables than nominal tire width.
steps.warning: Never exceed the lowest applicable tire or rim pressure limit.
steps.check: Both tires are within documented limits and appropriate for the intended setup/conditions.

steps.title: Treat air loss as a symptom, not a sealant recipe
steps.instruction: If a tubeless system loses pressure abnormally, inspect for punctures, bead/rim-tape issues, valve problems or other visible leakage. Follow the actual tire/rim/sealant instructions for repair or sealant quantity.
steps.why: Different tubeless systems use different rim tape, valves, sealants and maintenance intervals.
steps.warning: Bike Atlas does not provide a universal sealant quantity or maintenance interval.
steps.check: Any abnormal pressure loss has been routed to the correct component-specific troubleshooting procedure.
